security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are benign animation identifiers, multilingual text, local media processing, or explicitly configured service access. An isolated runtime test confirmed specification-controlled JavaScript injection through the clip loader; rendering also disables browser origin protections. All 1,000 supplied findings were adjudicated; 494 omitted matches still require manual review before automatic publication. Static review was capped at 1000/1494 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 494 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: The clip loader evaluates sourceURL metadata containing an unvalidated grammar value.
remediation.suggestion: Map supported grammar identifiers to fixed module paths before fetching. Reject fragments, line terminators, and traversal; avoid eval and add malicious-spec regression tests.

remediation.issue: Rendering disables Chromium origin protections while serving local project files.
remediation.suggestion: Remove --disable-web-security, serve approved assets from one origin, and restrict renderer requests to approved local resources or explicitly authorized remote assets.

remediation.issue: The static catalog excludes 494 repeated or lower-priority matches.
remediation.suggestion: Complete manual adjudication of the omitted matches before enabling automatic publication. Keep this coverage limitation visible in the release audit.

content.user_title: Create Art Animations and Narrated Explainer Clips
content.value_statement: Producing consistent animated videos requires coordinated storyboards, visual styles, timing, and review. This skill combines reusable animation components, local rendering, and optional media workflows.
actual_capabilities: Break down reference videos into scene timing, motion mechanisms, and visual comparisons.
Build code-driven scenes using art-style recipes, camera helpers, drawing libraries, and transitions.
Render eight parameterized explainer grammars with timed cues, shared palettes, and configurable dimensions.
Export still frames, H.264 video, and transparent ProRes clips through Playwright and ffmpeg.
Check storyboards, text layout, rendering determinism, motion, blank frames, and delivery reports.
Reuse existing media, synthesize macOS system speech, or coordinate explicitly authorized speech cloning and host image tools.
limitations: Local rendering requires Python, Playwright Chromium, ffmpeg, and relevant optional dependencies.
Research style recipes have incomplete visual validation; some reference films require separately supplied character frames and audio.
Image generation depends on tools available in the current session; system speech is implemented only for macOS.
Untrusted clip specifications can inject browser JavaScript; the loader requires remediation before processing externally supplied specifications.

use_cases.title: Explain a Lesson Visually
use_cases.description: Turn a short lesson into whiteboard or mathematical animation clips with timed narration and checked text placement.

use_cases.title: Develop an Original Art Animation
use_cases.description: Study reference works, compare composition options, and adapt brushwork, palettes, and transitions to an original subject.

use_cases.title: Assemble a Narrated Report
use_cases.description: Combine supplied screenshots, charts, and recorded narration into consistent clips with technical QA and a delivery report.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Short Animation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a storyboard for a 12-second animation about [topic]. Use one palette and concrete objects. Do not render or use external services.

prompt_templates.title: Render a Supplied-Media Explainer
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my screenshots at [folder] to explain [topic] in three short clips. Create local specifications, preview stills, and layout checks. Keep cloud services off.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt an Art Style
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced: original scene design and comparison
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt [style] to an original scene about [subject]. Propose three compositions and distinguish implemented techniques from research recipes. Render the approved direction and compare stills.

prompt_templates.title: Produce a Reviewed Narrated Video
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a [duration]-second explainer from my script and recording at [paths]. Create original local specifications and consistent clips. Run technical QA and independent review. Deliver the video with an unchanged factual report. Do not process external specifications or enable paid services.

output_examples.input: Plan a 12-second explanation of bread freezing.
output: Illustrative storyboard: show sliced bread, separate portions, seal a bag, and place it in the freezer.
Use one palette across four shots, with short labels and varied framing.
Expected planning deliverables: a shot table, timing notes, and storyboard lint results.

output_examples.input: Prepare a chart animation using my quarterly revenue figures.
output: Illustrative sequence: establish axes, reveal the quarterly values, and highlight the largest change.
Expected render deliverables: preview stills, an MP4 clip, and text-layout diagnostics.
Source figures and axis labels remain subject to user verification.

output_examples.input: Review a completed narrated explainer before delivery.
output: Expected review deliverables: motion measurements, visual contact sheets, blank-frame timestamps, and text-placement warnings.
The delivery report records technical gate results and the presence or absence of independent review.
Human review remains necessary for factual accuracy, visual quality, and narration pronunciation.

best_practices: Approve a storyboard, palette, and representative still frames before rendering the complete video.
Use original local specifications and inspect every asset path; obtain separate consent for cloud processing, paid calls, and voice training.
Run technical checks and an independent review, then watch the complete video at normal speed.
anti_patterns: Rendering untrusted external specifications before the grammar-loader injection vulnerability is fixed.
Treating research recipes or automated QA results as proof of finished visual quality.
Copying demonstration characters, compositions, or restricted assets directly into a new production.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The package targets Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows. Available image tools and permissions depend on the current session.

faq.question: What must be installed for video rendering?
faq.answer: Rendering requires Python, Playwright with Chromium, and ffmpeg. Some analysis and media operations require additional optional libraries.

faq.question: Does it generate images by itself?
faq.answer: No. The Python tools prepare plans and validate outputs. The agent must invoke an available, authorized image tool or import existing images.

faq.question: Are cloud services required?
faq.answer: No. Existing images and recordings support local workflows. Cloud speech cloning requires configured credentials and explicit permissions.

faq.question: Are all documented styles fully implemented?
faq.answer: No. The library distinguishes implemented techniques from research recipes. Some demonstrations and reference films require additional assets or visual validation.

faq.question: Can I render specifications from other people?
faq.answer: Not safely without remediation. A crafted grammar value can execute browser JavaScript. Review specifications and restrict processing to trusted inputs.
